correctness.rationale: All section vertices from crossed cross-polytope edges are enumerated; symmetry makes diameter twice the maximum vertex norm, and the monotone ratio function selects extreme absolute normal coordinates. The conditioned Gaussian maximum gives the exact integral. Half-normal minima and Gaussian maxima, followed by Slutsky, give exponential rate 1/sqrt(pi); uniform exponential tails for n times the minimum plus a superpolynomially rare low-maximum event prove all fixed moment limits. Standalone code independently enumerates vertices and checks integral/Monte Carlo finite cases.

value.rationale: A complete CDF for a canonical high-dimensional convex-body random section has natural geometric meaning. The upper-edge deficit has sharp n sqrt(log n) scale, non-Gaussian exponential limit with explicit rate, and converging all positive integer moments; these quantify geometry unavailable from mere concentration bounds or one fixed-dimensional section table.
